hook: SCP-2460 opens as a dry orbital report about a dense, barely visible object circling the Earth, and its class line already tells you the Safe rating did not hold. It rewards patience, because the physics-heavy description is setting up a lecture at the end that explains everything in plain language. No science background is needed; the lecturer deliberately skips the math.
whyItMatters: This is hard science fiction in SCP form, where the anomaly gets explained rather than left mysterious, and the dread comes from finally understanding it. The Safe class sitting beside a Keter correction that points to an addendum is a compact example of how a file's header can carry plot. It also builds its end-of-the-world scenario from straightforward physical reasoning instead of any hostile intent.
thingsToNotice: The inventory is the eeriest part: among the rocks sit a comet nucleus, an alien vessel with two long-dead crocodile-like crew, and ninety capsules each holding a desiccated humanoid, all overlapping in one place. A stray bolt shows how quickly contact takes effect, and the probe mission confirms it when the agent's thrusters fire uselessly through his own hull and he falls into the mass, joining that same list. The lecture then reveals an invisible cloud reaching kilometers past the visible core and describes how a decaying orbit would let the object swing back and forth through the planet until Earth collapses into untouchable rubble. The last lines name the thing as dark matter and flip the question around: considering how much of it the universe holds, the real surprise is that we have not run into it sooner.
